chunks: My father, Muhammad b. al-Hasan, and Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar — may God be pleased with them — narrated to us. They said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Musa b. Bashshar al-Attar, from al-Mas'udi, from Abdullah b. al-Zubayr, from Aban b. Taghlub, al-Rabi' b. Sulayman, Aban b. Arqam, and others.

They said: We set out from Mecca until, when we were in the valley of al-Ajfar, we came upon a man who was praying while we could still see the rays of the sun. We felt displeasure within ourselves. He continued praying while we were supplicating against him, until he had prayed one unit of prayer while we were supplicating against him and saying: This one is from the youth of the people of Medina. But when we approached him, it turned out to be Abu Abdullah Ja'far b. Muhammad — peace be upon them both. So we dismounted and prayed with him.
We had missed one unit. When we completed the prayer, we stood and went to him, saying: May we be made your sacrifice! You pray at this hour? He said: Once the sun sets, the time has entered.

key_terms.دخل الوقت: The time has entered — the prescribed window for performing the obligatory prayer has begun
key_terms.ركعة: A single unit of prayer (rak'ah) consisting of standing, bowing, and two prostrations
key_terms.صلاة المغرب: The Maghrib (sunset) prayer, the fourth of the five daily obligatory prayers in Islam
key_terms.وادي الأجفر: The valley of al-Ajfar, a location on the route between Mecca and Medina where this encounter took place

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Companions traveling from Mecca encountered a man praying Maghrib in the Ajfar valley while sunlight was still visible, which they considered premature. They cursed him, assuming he was an ignorant youth from Medina. Upon approaching, they discovered it was Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as). Humbled, they joined his prayer, missing one unit. When they questioned the timing, the Imam clarified that once the sun's disc disappears below the horizon, the prayer time has begun — regardless of remaining rays in the sky. This hadith was understood by the original audience as an authoritative jurisprudential ruling from the Imam, settling the common dispute about whether Maghrib begins at the disappearance of the disc or the fading of the redness.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father and Muhammad b. al-Hasan and Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar (ra) narrated to us. They said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad b. al-Husayn from Abi’l Khattab from Musa b. Bashar al-`Attar from al-Mas`udi from `Abdullah b. al-Zubayr from Aban b. Taghlub and al-Rabi` b. Sulayman and Aban b. Arqam and others.

They said: We proceeded from Mecca until we reached the Ajfar valley, where we came across a man who was praying. We saw the rays of the Sun, so we felt angry. He was praying whilst we were supplicating against him. He prayed one unit whilst we were supplicating against him; we were saying: He is from the youth of the people of the Medina. When we came to him, it turned out that he was Abu `Abdillah Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). So, we descended and prayed with him.

We had missed one unit; so, when we completed the prayer, we stood and went to him, saying: May we be your sacrifice! Is this the time that you pray? So, he said: Once the Sun sets, then the time has begun.
